transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess... I came in because I've started doing some things lately that kind of scare me. Just... I don't know. Walking out in the middle of system deployments at work, or... driving around late at night with no real plan. It's... that's just not how I've ever handled stress before. So... yeah.
Have you been feeling anxious lately?
Um... I don't know if I'd use the word anxious. I guess I just feel... stressed out. It's hard to say.
Have you been acting on impulse more often than usual?

Um... I guess that's what I meant earlier. With the driving, or just... leaving work like that. I don't really plan it out, I just do it. And... yeah, it kind of scares me, because I've just never been the type to do things like that.
Have you recently engaged in any behaviors that could potentially harm yourself or others?

Um... I mean, mostly just what I already said. The... driving around in the dark without a plan. I guess that could be dangerous. And just walking out during a deployment... it scares me because I've just never handled things this way before. That's... that's really it.
Have you always been someone who acts on impulse, or is this a recent change for you?

No... like I said, it's a recent change. I've never handled stress this way before. That's... kind of why I came in, actually. Because starting to do things that scare me, like the driving late at night or walking out on deployments... it's just not who I am.
Have you always been someone who has difficulty following rules or conforming to social norms?
No... not at all. I've always followed the rules. Like I keep saying, this is all just... new. I don't usually act like this.
Have you always felt like you have to do things your own way?
No, I... I don't think so. I've always been pretty good about just doing what's expected of me. I'm not... I'm not really a rebel or anything.
Are these recent changes causing problems in your daily life or relationships?

Yeah... I guess they are. I, um... I just had my performance review at work. It was the first time I've ever been told that I'm missing key handoffs. They said I keep leaving meetings abruptly... that the team is having to work around me. And... well, at home, my husband says it feels like I'm barely present anymore. So... yes.
Are you feeling overwhelmed or emotionally distressed most of the time?

I guess so. Um... even on the quiet days, there's just this... this feeling sitting in my chest. It's hard to explain. Just a mix of fear and... I don't know, maybe shame. Like I should have handled everything better. And... I just feel like if I let my guard down, something else could happen. So... yeah.
Has something traumatic happened to you recently?

Yes. Um... there was an incident. I... I'd really rather not go into the details of what happened that night, if that's okay. But... I guess it's why, out of nowhere, especially in the conference area at work... or if someone just raises their voice on a call... I'll get hit with these images and sounds from that night. It hits so strongly that I just... I completely lose track of what I was saying.
Did the incident that happened trigger these changes in your behavior?
Yeah... I think so. It all started after that late-night cutover incident. That was... um, a little over a year ago. About 13 months now, I guess. So, yes.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities since the incident?

Yeah... I suppose I do. I mean... I take the long way around the building now. I just avoid that floor whenever I can. And... if people start talking about the contractor, or the cutover... I just shut the conversation down. I don't really want to be around any of that.
Do you experience memories or images from the incident that intrude into your mind when you're not trying to think about them?

Yeah... like I mentioned earlier. Um... it just happens out of nowhere. If I have to be near that conference area, or... if someone gets loud on a call, those pictures and noises just kind of force their way in. I'm not trying to think about it, but it... it hits hard enough that I just completely lose my train of thought.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body or watching yourself from afar?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really felt anything like that.
